points.text: Escalating geopolitical tensions and renewed U.S. tariff threats at the start of June drove spot gold up over 2%, marking a sharp rally.
Investor safe‑haven demand spiked after Israel's strike on Iran, pushing gold to its highest level in more than a month by mid‑June.
Indian gold prices rose steadily through early and mid‑June, mirroring the global safe‑haven rally.
A ceasefire ending the 12‑day Iran‑Israel war later in the month improved risk appetite, sending gold down more than 1% to a near two‑week low.

months.why_it_matters: Gold’s price swings highlighted how quickly investor sentiment reacts to geopolitical shocks and subsequent de‑escalation, influencing safe‑haven demand and broader market risk assessments.

Mid‑month prices fell, pressured by a firmer dollar, improving global trade sentiment and a U.S. tariff threat on copper, which dragged down mining shares.
Persistent trade‑related uncertainties, especially U.S.–EU negotiations and fresh U.S. tariff announcements, lifted safe‑haven demand and helped gold rebound from a one‑month low by month‑end.
Analysts warned that after a multi‑year rally, gold may enter a consolidation phase as many of the up‑trend drivers are now priced in.

A brief lift in gold prices was triggered by weaker‑than‑expected U.S. labor revisions and fleeting geopolitical headlines, showing the metal’s sensitivity to short‑term macro news.
In India, gold breached ₹1.11 lakh per 10 grams ahead of key U.S. inflation data and Fed comments, reflecting the global impact of U.S. monetary expectations on local markets.

months.why_it_matters: The sharp rise in gold underscores investor anxiety over monetary policy and currency weakness, while its outperformance of other assets highlights a shift toward safe‑haven demand. Record levels also signal potential spill‑over effects on emerging‑market economies reliant on gold pricing.

months.headline: Gold prices surged to record highs in early October then suffered a sharp correction by month‑end

points.text: Gold prices surged to fresh record highs in early October, with Indian gold hitting a lifetime high of Rs 1,26,600 per 10 g and global prices approaching $4,000 per ounce, as investors reacted to the US government shutdown and political unrest in France.

The rally continued through mid‑month, driven by expectations of further Fed rate cuts, concerns over US tariffs and ongoing US‑China trade tensions, pushing XAU/USD to near $4,240 and MCX December futures up more than ₹2,000 (over 1.6%).

months.why_it_matters: The episode underscores gold’s function as a safe‑haven asset during geopolitical and monetary uncertainty, while also highlighting the rapid volatility that can affect investors, lenders and broader financial markets.

months.headline: Gold prices swung between declines and rallies in November 2025, driven by China policy moves, US shutdown uncertainty, and weaker US data.

points.text: Early‑month expectations of a major spike in Indian gold prices were sparked by a Chinese policy decision, while broader market fears lifted gold amid the record‑long US shutdown.
The resolution of the US government shutdown lifted gold, with prices edging higher after the funding bill was signed and the XAU/USD rallying to around $4,195 ahead of the shutdown‑ending vote.

Later in the month weaker‑than‑expected US data sparked a rebound, sending December futures up 1.3% to a new intraday high, after a prior three‑week decline caused by a stronger dollar and fading Fed‑cut hopes.

months.why_it_matters: These moves show how geopolitical cues and US fiscal‑policy uncertainty can quickly shift investor demand for gold, affecting global markets and inflation‑hedge strategies.

months.headline: Gold prices surged to record highs in December 2025, breaching $4,500 per ounce as global uncertainty and strong demand drove a sharp rally.

points.text: Spot gold crossed the $4,500‑ounce mark for the first time, as investors sought safety amid geopolitical uncertainty and expectations of interest‑rate cuts by major central banks.
The rally built on earlier momentum, with gold having already topped $4,000 an ounce in 2025 and the forces behind the surge remaining strong in both the near and long term.
Domestic demand in India stayed firm, pushing rates higher across major Indian cities and keeping the gold market on a steady uptrend at the start of the month.

months.why_it_matters: The unprecedented price levels highlight gold’s role as a safe‑haven asset amid heightened geopolitical tension and anticipated monetary easing, while drawing significant investor inflows and reinforcing demand in key markets such as India.

months.headline: Gold price swung wildly in February 2026, dropping below $5,000 amid easing US‑China tensions before rebounding on safe‑haven demand and macro data.

points.text: Early February forecasts highlighted a historic 2025 surge, but optimism from a Trump‑Xi call eased geopolitical tension and sent gold below $5,000.
Mid‑month gold fell sharply, ending an unprecedented rally as the US dollar rebounded and safe‑haven demand waned.
Late February gold regained momentum, supported by Q4 GDP and PCE figures that justified a hold on Fed policy and by persistent US‑Iran tensions.

Analysts debated the broader macro backdrop—US debt trust, low inflation and interest rates, dollar hegemony, and a potential $5,500 ceiling—while India’s budget focus kept regional gold demand in view.

months.why_it_matters: The February volatility shows how quickly gold reacts to shifts in geopolitical relations, US monetary policy cues, and emerging market demand, signaling the metal’s role as a barometer for global risk sentiment.

months.headline: Gold prices swung between brief gains and sharp regional declines, ending the month in a sideways consolidation.

points.text: Early April saw divergent moves: Indian gold fell 1.5% while global spot gold rose 2.3% after a US‑Iran de‑escalation, showing sensitivity to geopolitical news.
Mid‑month, easing tensions and unchanged Fed policy triggered a sharp sell‑off in China, with gold down over 15%, reflecting a broader global precious‑metals decline.
By late April, rising oil prices and renewed US‑Iran frictions pushed spot gold down modestly in Asia, and the market entered a broad sideways range as inflation and tight monetary expectations loom.
Analysts warned that the ongoing US‑Iran conflict could shave 0.7% off the global economy, boosting gold as investors eye a larger US deficit and a weaker dollar.

months.why_it_matters: The month’s price swings highlight how quickly geopolitical events, regional market pressures, and monetary‑policy outlooks can shift safe‑haven demand for gold, influencing investor portfolios and broader economic sentiment.

months.headline: Gold prices swung amid geopolitical tensions, shaping economies and sparking environmental concerns

points.text: Gold prices rose over 1% early in the month on a weaker dollar and easing oil prices, then fell mid‑month as Middle East uncertainty, higher oil and stronger U.S. inflation data dampened hopes for Fed rate cuts, ending the month below $4,600.
Surging gold prices helped Tanzania cushion the impact of rising oil costs from the Middle East conflict, keeping its current‑account deficit projected below three percent despite external pressures.
The recent gold price surge has reignited a mining rush in Brazil’s Amazon rainforest, accelerating deforestation in protected areas and driving hazardous mercury contamination.

months.why_it_matters: Gold’s volatility influences inflation expectations and central‑bank policy while providing a financial buffer for vulnerable economies, and the price‑driven mining boom threatens critical ecosystems and public health.

data.arc: June 2025 saw gold rally on heightened geopolitical risk, but a cease‑fire quickly pulled prices lower. Throughout the summer and into autumn, trade tensions, dollar moves and expectations of Fed rate cuts pushed the metal to successive record highs, culminating in the $4,500‑plus levels of December 2025. Early 2026 the market surged to historic highs as geopolitical shocks and policy uncertainty intensified, only to collapse in March 2026 into a 40‑year low as investors fled the safe‑haven amid rising oil prices and inflation fears. By April and May 2026 the price action steadied into a sideways range, reflecting a tug‑of‑war between easing tensions and persistent macro‑economic pressures.

turning_points.why: Geopolitical tensions and a Middle East cease‑fire drove a sharp rally followed by a rapid slip as risk appetite improved.
Investors bet on Fed rate cuts and a weaker dollar, sending gold to record highs and highlighting its sensitivity to short‑term macro news.
Geopolitical turmoil, including the US capture of Venezuela’s leader, and policy uncertainty spurred a surge to historic highs.
A sharp rally collapsed into a historic plunge, turning gold from a safe‑haven into a volatile commodity amid soaring oil, inflation fears and expectations of prolonged high US rates.

watch: Future Fed policy decisions and their impact on dollar strength
Developments in US‑Iran and US‑China relations that could reignite safe‑haven demand

meta_analysis.why: pools multiple studies and reports a combined estimate

guideline.why: a body reviewing the whole evidence base issued a recommendation

trial.why: randomised or controlled — the design that can establish an effect

observational.why: measures association in a real population; confounding is possible

review.why: summarises a field rather than adding a measurement

methodological.why: proposes a method rather than a finding about the world

theoretical.why: argues from theory rather than from data

case_report.why: one case; cannot support a general claim

patent.why: evidence that somebody is building it, not that it works
